and a Variance (PLNG2019-0044) requesting to reduce the required on-site parking, for
a new restaurant located at 22213-22215 Norwalk Boulevard, in the City of Hawaiian
Gardens.

After a careful review of the proposals, staff deemed the applications complete on
August 15, 2019. On August 16, 2019, staff mailed a notice of the pending public
hearing to all property owners within 300 feet of the subject site and the notice was
published in the Los Cerritos Community News.
   P. 13

 BACKGROUND

The subject property is located at the northwest corner of Norwalk Boulevard and 223 rd
Street. The site is located within the C-4 (General Commercial) Zoning District, with a
General Plan designation of "General Commercial". This general plan designation is
classified by commercial uses, including retail and restaurant uses that offer alcoholic
beverages, subject to the approval of a conditional use permit application.

Being generally rectangular in shape the site exhibits approximately 150 feet of frontage
on Norwalk Boulevard and approximately 177.8 feet of frontage on 223 rd Street. Two
buildings exist on the commercial center since 1993; a 2,914 square foot clothing store
and a 7,493 multi-tenant building where the subject restaurant is located. Surrounding
land uses include residential developments to the south and west, and general
retail/service to the north and east.

DISCUSSION/ANALYSIS

 Under these (CUP and Variance) applications, the applicant is requesting the Planning
Commission's approval of a CUP to allow the sale and consumption of alcoholic
beverages to patrons. Without the sales of alcoholic beverages, restaurants and food
stores are permitted as principal uses within the C-4 zone. Also, the applicant is asking
for approval to reduce the number of required parking spaces. Per City's code,
restaurant uses require more parking than retail businesses. The applicant plans to
convert the existing 1,948 square feet office/retail spaces into restaurant use; as a
result, it triggers the requirement for more parking. The applicant stated his desire to
establish a family-style restaur;:mt that has never been offered at the site and at the
immediate vicinity. There will be no bar area and no live music entertainment at the
establishment. Following is an analysis of these aspects of the applications:

Conditional Use Permit for Alcoholic Beverages

Section 18.100.090.D of the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code stipulates that the
 Planning Commission shall consider applications for a Conditional Use Permit and may,
when such conditions are found necessary, approve the use, provided the use will not
jeopardize, adversely affect, endanger, or otherwise constitute a menace to the public
health, safety, or general welfare, or be materially detrimental to the property of other
persons located in the vicinity of such use. As such, an approval of the proposed
conditional use permit would allow the applicant to sell and consume alcoholic
beverages in conjunction with the restaurant, under the guidelines for a Type 41
Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control license. A Type 41 license and its basic
privileges are described as follows:

  "On-Sale Beer and Wine - Eating Place - (Restaurant) Authorizes the sale of beer
  and wine for consumption on the premises where sold. Distilled spirits may not be on
  the premises (except brandy, rum, or liqueurs for use solely for cooking purposes).
  Must operate and maintain the licensed premises as a bona fide eating place. Must
  maintain suitable kitchen facilities, and must make actual and substantial sales of
  meals for consumption on the premises. Minors are allowed on the premises."
   P. 14

The operation that the applicant proposes will satisfy this requirement. The applicant
stated that the request would allow the restaurant to increase its sales revenues
significantly. It is important to note that alcohol shall only be served within the confines
of the restaurant; as such, no alcohol will be served outdoors or outside of the premises.
In observing the subject commercial center and its surrounding area, staff notices there
is only one liquor store that operates with an ABC license (Type 21 off-sale general) and
is located within 300' from the subject tenant space. Staff believes approving another
ABC license in conjunction with a restaurant at the subject site would allow the applicant
an opportunity to revitalize the commercial center.

The restaurant's hours of operation are as follows:
  • Sunday, Monday-Thursday:  8:00 am to 11 :00 pm
  • Friday and Saturday:  8:00 am to 3:00 am*
*The sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages shall be prohibited between the hours of 2:00 a.m.
and 6:00 a.m. daily

LA County Sheriff's Department Report

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department (LACSD) was contacted regarding the
potential establishment of an alcohol license at the subject business. The Sheriff's
Department stated that they had no objection to the establishment of the alcohol use in
conjunction with the restaurant. However, the Sheriff's Department is concerned about
the 3:00 a.m. closing on Fridays and Saturdays. Staff has reviewed the proposed hours
of operation and concurred with LACSD's concern. As such, staff recommends that the
12:00 midnight closing time would be appropriate for this family-style restaurant.

Public Convenience and Necessity

Business and Professions Code Section 23958.4 stipulates that the State Alcohol
Beverage Control (ABC) may grant a license to an applicant if the "local governing body
of the area in which they are located determines that public convenience or necessity
would be served by the issuance of the license.

The finding of public convenience or necessity is to be made in areas of "undue
concentration" which, pursuant to Section 23958.4, is related to the number of existing
liquor licenses and reported crime within the crime reporting districts of the law
enforcement agency.

Undue Concentration of Liquor Licenses

An undue concentration exists when the ratio of on-sale and off-site licenses to
population in the census tract in which the premises are located exceeds the ratio of
licenses to population in the county. The conditional use permit proposes to establish
the alcohol use at 22213-22215 Norwalk Boulevard which is located within census tract
5552.11. The total population of the census tract is currently 5,818. A total of four (4)
liquor licenses are permitted before ABC considers the tract to have an "undue
concentration". Currently the tract has a total of two (2) active on-sale licenses.
   P. 1 5

In evaluating the application, staff supports the request for the sale and consumption of
alcoholic beverages in conjunction with the restaurant. However, to mitigate any
potential impacts and to avoid future problems, staff is recommending the following
conditions of approval for the business:

  1. Customers shall not gather in the restaurant's parking lot area after closing time.
  2. No live entertainment and no live music (i.e. karaoke, live band, disc jockey,
  dancing, and coin-operated amusement devices) are allowed at any times.

Variance to Reduce Required Parking

The commercial center where the current business is located has 37 parking stalls.
Section 18. 70.01 0 (Parking) of the Hawaiian Gardens Municipal Code stipulates that
one parking space is required for every 100 square feet of gross floor area for full
service sit-down restaurants. The proposed 1,958 sq. ft. restaurant requires 20 parking
spaces, which is 12 spaces more than the previous retail business at 8 spaces (1 space
per 250 sq. ft.). The entire commercial center with a new restaurant requires 54 spaces,
whereas the site only has 37 spaces. As such, the applicant is not able to provide
sufficient parking to comply with today's code.

 to deviate from the Zoning Code, which will allow the applicant to accomplish his plan
 by opening his first family-style restaurant.

 In observing the subject commercial center, particularly to the larger tenant spaces, staff
 notices the Mother's Nutritional Center closes at 7:00 p.m. on weekday, at 4:00 p.m. on
 Saturday, and closed on Sunday. The family clothing store is also operating at the
 similar hours to the Mother's Nutritional Center. The early closing time on the weekend
 for these businesses will help create additional parking spaces; thus, accommodate the
 need for more parking at the restaurant. Staff believes that approving the variance
 allows the applicant to fill the tenant space that has been vacant for months. Also, it is
 staff's opinion that the proposed use will attract patrons to the area and help revive the
 commercial center. With conditions of approval in place, staff feels that the project will

 FINDINGS

Pursuant to HGMC Section 18.100.100E, there are five (5) findings that must be
adopted prior to the Planning Commission approving the Variance. A discussion of the
findings follows:

1.  That the variance is consistent with the Hawaiian Gardens General Plan and
  other applicable City policies and regulations and that there would be no
  adverse impacts on the environment.
  Allowing the variance would be consistent with the Hawaiian Gardens General
  Plan and Zoning Ordinance. In particular, the variance would allow the
  commercial center to proceed and operate with 37 parking spaces, consistent
  with the following General Plan Goals and Policies:
  Land Use Element- Policy 4.6- Suppo,t redevelopment of underutilized and blighted
  commercial areas along Norwalk Boulevard.

  The variance will provide the applicant an opportunity to occupy a vacant space
  that has been vacant for a long time and the business will help attract patrons to
  the area. The proposed restaurant will complement the surrounding uses.
  Land Use Element- Policy 4.7- Provide neighborhood commercial uses throughout
  the community to make goods and services available within walking distances of
  residents.

  Approving the variance will allow the applicant to establish a business that has
  never been offered to the site and the immediate commercial and residential areas.
  The restaurant will add excitement and revive the commercial center.

2.  That there are exceptional or extraordinary circumstances or conditions
  applicable to the subject property which do not apply generally to other
  properties in the same zone in which the project is located.
   P. 18

  The subject site is conducive to the proposed restaurant, as it meets or exceeds
  all applicable development standards in the C-4 zone, except for the parking
  standard for which the applicant has requested variance. It is staff's opinion,
  based on substantial evidence that other existing businesses don't operate after
  7:00 p.m. on weekday, 4:00 p.m. on Saturday, and closed on Sunday. That
  leaves amber parking available for patrons to the restaurant. In addition, staff
  isn't anticipating a significant parking increased for the 1,948 sq. ft. restaurant
  than the retail use.

3.  That the granting of the Variance will not constitute a grant of special
  privilege inconsistent with the limitations on other properties in the same
  zone with similar constraints.

  The variance is needed to reduce the required parking from 54 to 37 spaces for
  the commercial center. Approving the variance will not constitute a grant of
  special privilege inconsistent with the limitations on other properties in the same
  zone. As mentioned previously, with the early closing time for the adjoining
  businesses at the site, there will be sufficient parking spaces available. Similar
  variances were granted for a church facility (Iglesia Central church) located on
  Hawaiian Avenue and the Self-Storage facility located on Carson Street.

3.  That the Variance is made on the basis of a hardship condition and not as a
  matter of convenience or cost.
  The proposed 37 parking spaces instead of 54 will provide sufficient parking spaces
  for patrons since the restaurant will not always fully occupied. The project does not
  involve the expansion of the building footprint. Thus, this does not require the
  increase for additional parking spaces. However, the applicant is creating an
  inviting eating establishment that attracts clientele and revives the commercial
  center. It is staff's opinion that the request for parking reduction is reasonable
  since the project meets or exceeds all other development standards.

4.  That the granting of the Variance will not be detrimental to the public health,
  safety, or welfare or materially injurious to properties or improvements in the
  vicinity.
  The project will not be detrimental to the public health, safety, or welfare or
  materially injurious to properties or improvements in the vicinity since the new
  restaurant will be a major improvement to the subject center; indeed, the proposed
  project would benefit the City as a whole by filling a vacant tenant space, and
  increasing the City's economic vitality.

  Furthermore, with all the parking spaces located at the front and between the
  buildings, the property still has adequate turning movements that allow patrons to
  maneuver throughout the parking lot.
   P. 19

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

Staff has reviewed the proposed project for compliance with the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Upon completion of this review, staff determined
that this request is categorically exempt from CEQA, pursuant to Guideline Section No.
15301 (Class 1, Existing Facilities). Categorical Exemptions are projects, which have
been determined not to have a significant effect on the environment and have been
exempted from the requirements of the CEQA. It is staff's opinion that the request to
operate with an ABC license at the existing tenant space and to reduce the required
parking spaces will not result in any changes in land use; thereby qualifying for the
Class 1 exemption.

As of the date that this report was printed, staff has not received any correspondence
regarding this matter.
